ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the isosceles right triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $E$ is a point on the side $AC$ (not coinciding with the endpoints), a line is drawn through point $E$ such that $EG \perp BC$ at point $G$, and $EH \perp AD$ at point $H$, a line is drawn through point $B$ such that $BF \parallel AC$ intersecting the extension of $EG$ at point $F$. If $AG=3$, what is the area of the shaded region?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $DG=a$, $CG=b$, then $CD=a+b$, \\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=45^\circ$, $AB=AC$, \\
also since $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, \\
thus $BD=AD=CD=a+b$, $BC=2BD=2(a+b)$, \\
since $EG\perp BC$, $EH\perp AD$, \\
thus quadrilateral DGEH is a rectangle, $\angle GEC=45^\circ$, \\
thus $DH=EG=CG=b$, \\
since $BF\parallel AC$, \\
thus $\angle FBG=\angle ACB=45^\circ$, \\
since $EF\perp BC$, \\
thus $\angle F=45^\circ$, \\
thus $GF=BG=BD+DG=a+b+a=2a+b$, \\
by the Pythagorean theorem, $AD^2+DG^2=AG^2$, \\
thus $(a+b)^2+a^2=9$, \\
which simplifies to $2a^2+2ab+b^2=9$, \\
According to the problem, ${S}_{\text{shaded}}={S}_{\triangle ABC}+{S}_{\triangle BGF}-{S}_{\text{rectangle} DGEH}$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AD+\frac{1}{2}BG\cdot GF-DG\cdot DH$\\
$=BD\cdot AD+\frac{1}{2}BG^2-DG\cdot DH$\\
$=(a+b)^2+\frac{1}{2}(2a+b)^2-ab$\\
$=a^2+2ab+b^2+2a^2+ab+\frac{1}{2}b^2-ab$\\
$=\frac{3}{2}(2a^2+2ab+b^2)$\\
$=\frac{3}{2}\times 9$\\
$=\boxed{13.5}$

D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse BC, so in the right triangle D is equidistant from A, B, C, namely AD=BD=CD=a+b, and BC=2(a+b).

Since EG⊥BC, EH⊥AD, and in this isosceles right triangle AD⊥BC, DGEH is a rectangle. Also because AC and BC form 45°, E is on AC, and EG⊥BC, so right triangle EGC is a 45-45-90 triangle, EG=CG=b. In the rectangle DH=EG=b, therefore the area of rectangle DGEH is DG·DH=ab.

=1/2·BC·AD+1/2·BG·GF-DG·DH
=(a+b)^2+1/2(2a+b)^2-ab.

(a+b)^2+1/2(2a+b)^2-ab
=a^2+2ab+b^2+2a^2+2ab+1/2b^2-ab
=3a^2+3ab+3/2b^2
=3/2(2a^2+2ab+b^2)
=3/2((a+b)^2+a^2).
From (a+b)^2+a^2=9, obtain the shaded area S=3/2×9=13.5.
